key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though many point defects create deep gap states, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic efficiency losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where defect tolerance can relax material purity requirements and simplify device optimization.
method: First-principles calculations of point defects in trigonal selenium
Computed defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination via nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture
Surveyed a large, chemically diverse defect set across charge states, level positions, lattice relaxation, and doping conditions
evidence_signal: Across the defect dataset, recombination is strongly suppressed by large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per event, indicating realistic defect concentrations cannot account for the measured efficiency limits.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on idealized first-principles defect models, so real devices may still be affected by extended defects, interfaces, or processing-induced degradation not captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
